<!-- DO NOT EDIT | GENERATED CONTENT -->

Installs a unit that runs 'vllm-helper restart' at boot and 'vllm-helper stop' on
shutdown. The unit names no recipe: which one runs comes from the active profile,
so switching recipes does not mean editing the unit.

## Usage

```console
vllm-helper recipes install-service [flags]
```

## Options

### --name

|         |                                   |
| ------- | --------------------------------- |
| Type    | <code>string</code>               |
| Default | <code>vllm-cluster.service</code> |

systemd unit name

### --now

|      |                   |
| ---- | ----------------- |
| Type | <code>bool</code> |

enable and start the service immediately

### --supersede-native

|         |                   |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| Type    | <code>bool</code> |
| Default | <code>true</code> |

stop and disable the single-node unit this replaces

### --timeout

|         |                   |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| Type    | <code>int</code>  |
| Default | <code>1800</code> |

seconds to allow for the model to load

### --user

|      |                     |
| ---- | ------------------- |
| Type | <code>string</code> |

user the launcher runs as

### --watchdog

|         |                   |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| Type    | <code>bool</code> |
| Default | <code>true</code> |

also install a timer that relaunches the cluster when the endpoint stops answering

### --watchdog-interval

|         |                  |
| ------- | ---------------- |
| Type    | <code>int</code> |
| Default | <code>2</code>   |

minutes between health checks
